level1.text: A runner moves at a uniform velocity along a straight track and covers $120\,\text{m}$ in $15\,\text{s}$ in the direction chosen as positive. What is the runner's velocity?
A cart on the $x$-axis is first at the position $12\,\text{m}$ and then moves to the position $-5.0\,\text{m}$. What is the displacement of the cart? Give the answer with its sign.
A cart moves at a uniform velocity of $3.5\,\text{m/s}$ in the positive direction for $12\,\text{s}$. How large is the displacement of the cart?
The $(t, x)$ graph of a cart is a straight line that passes through the points $(0\,\text{s};\, 4.0\,\text{m})$ and $(10\,\text{s};\, 24\,\text{m})$. What is the velocity of the cart?

At the moment $t = 0\,\text{s}$ a walker is at the position $15\,\text{m}$ and walks uniformly at a velocity $1.5\,\text{m/s}$ in the positive direction. At what position is she at the moment $t = 20\,\text{s}$?
The $(t, x)$ graph of an object is a straight line that falls from left to right. What does this tell about the motion of the object?
level1.answer: The position decreases as time passes, so the velocity is negative and the motion is in the negative direction.

choices.text: The position decreases as time passes, so the velocity is negative and the motion is in the negative direction.
choices.feedback: Correct: the slope of the line is the velocity, and the slope of a falling line is negative. The sign tells the direction of the motion.

choices.text: The object is moving downhill, because the graph goes downwards and the graph shows the shape of the path.
choices.feedback: The graph is not a picture of the path. It shows position as a function of time, and an object can move along a horizontal track even though the graph falls.

choices.text: The object is coming to a stop, because the line of the graph tilts and the magnitude of the velocity decreases.
choices.feedback: A stopped object is at rest, and its graph is horizontal. A straight line whose slope does not change describes a constant velocity, not a slowing motion.

choices.text: As time passes the object moves backwards in time, because the position values of the graph get smaller.
choices.feedback: Time always increases as one goes to the right. A decreasing position means motion in the negative direction, not travelling backwards in time.

level1.text: A walker walks $40\,\text{m}$ east along a straight road, turns around and walks the same $40\,\text{m}$ back to the starting point. East has been chosen as the positive direction. Which statement about the whole walk is correct?
level1.answer: The displacement is $0\,\text{m}$, because the final position is the same as the initial position.

choices.text: The displacement is $0\,\text{m}$, because the final position is the same as the initial position.
choices.feedback: Correct: the displacement is the final position minus the initial position. The distance travelled does not affect it, and here the distance is $80\,\text{m}$.

choices.text: The displacement is $80\,\text{m}$, because the displacement is the whole length of the route travelled.
choices.feedback: The length of the route is the distance, not the displacement. The displacement depends only on the initial and final positions, and here they are the same.

choices.text: The displacement is $40\,\text{m}$, because only the outward leg counts when the motion turns around.
choices.feedback: The whole motion affects the displacement. The return leg moves the walker back $40\,\text{m}$, so it cancels the outward leg.

choices.text: The displacement is $-40\,\text{m}$, because the last leg goes in the negative direction.
choices.feedback: The sign belongs to the whole displacement, not to the last leg. The displacement of the whole walk is zero, because the displacements of the legs, $+40\,\text{m}$ and $-40\,\text{m}$, add up to zero.

level1.text:
A student calculates the velocity of a cart from a straight line of the $(t, x)$ graph, whose points are $(2.0\,\text{s};\, 5.0\,\text{m})$ and $(6.0\,\text{s};\, 13\,\text{m})$.

The student's solution: $v = \dfrac{13\,\text{m}}{6.0\,\text{s}} = 2.2\,\text{m/s}$.

What is the error in the student's solution?
level1.answer: She divided the position of the second point by its time, although one must divide the change in position by the change in time.

choices.text: She divided the position of the second point by its time, although one must divide the change in position by the change in time.
choices.feedback: Correct: the velocity is the slope $\frac{x_2 - x_1}{t_2 - t_1}$. The differences between the points are $8.0\,\text{m}$ and $4.0\,\text{s}$, so the velocity is $2.0\,\text{m/s}$.

choices.text: She calculated speed and not velocity, because velocity is obtained from the sum of the positions divided by the sum of the times.
choices.feedback: A sum does not describe motion. The velocity is the change in position divided by the change in time, and a change is always a difference: final minus initial.

choices.text: She swapped the points, so the sign is wrong and the correct velocity is $-2.2\,\text{m/s}$.
choices.feedback: The position increases as time passes, so the velocity is positive. The value $2.2\,\text{m/s}$ is wrong already because the differences were not calculated.

choices.text: There is no error, because the velocity is the final position divided by the total time elapsed since the beginning.
choices.feedback: That would hold only if the motion started from the origin at the moment zero. Here the starting point is $(2.0\,\text{s};\, 5.0\,\text{m})$, so the differences must be taken.

level1.text:
A toy car moves along a straight track on the $x$-axis. At the moment $t = 0$ it is at the position $x_0 = 6.0\,\text{m}$.

The velocity of the car is $v = -1.0\,\text{m/s}$ all the time.

Which graph shows the position $x$ of the toy car as a function of time $t$ from the moment $0$ to the moment $4.0\,\text{s}$?

choices.feedback: Here the position grows by $1.0\,\text{m}$ every second, so the velocity would be $+1.0\,\text{m/s}$. The sign of the velocity has been ignored: the minus sign tells the direction, so the position must decrease.
The slope $-1.0\,\text{m/s}$ of the line is right, but the line starts from the origin. The initial position has been forgotten: at the moment $t = 0$ the graph must be at $x_0 = 6.0\,\text{m}$.
Correct: the line starts from $6.0\,\text{m}$ and falls $1.0\,\text{m}$ every second, so at the moment $4.0\,\text{s}$ the position is $2.0\,\text{m}$.
This is drawn like a $(t, v)$ graph: the value $-1.0$ is the velocity, not the position. A horizontal line in a $(t, x)$ graph would mean that the car stays at rest at $-1.0\,\text{m}$.

level2.text: A car drives along a straight road at a uniform velocity $90\,\text{km/h}$. How far does it travel in $12\,\text{s}$? Give the answer in metres.
A runner moves along a straight path at a uniform velocity of $4.0\,\text{m/s}$. How many minutes does it take her to cover a distance of $1.2\,\text{km}$?

At the moment $t = 2.0\,\text{s}$ a cart is at the position $18\,\text{m}$ and at the moment $t = 7.0\,\text{s}$ at the position $3.0\,\text{m}$. The cart moves uniformly. Calculate the velocity of the cart with its sign.

At the moment $t = 0\,\text{s}$ a cart is at the position $-24\,\text{m}$ and moves uniformly at a velocity $1.5\,\text{m/s}$ in the positive direction. When is the cart at the origin, that is at the position $x = 0$?

The motion of a cart was followed with video analysis. The table gives the position of the cart at different moments (example data). The motion of the cart is uniform.

Draw the $(t, x)$ graph from the data and fit a straight line through the points. Use the line to determine the velocity $v$ of the cart. Also give the initial position $x_0$ and write the position of the cart as a function of time.

Write the velocity in the answer box.

level2.text:
Two carts move along the same straight track and both motions are uniform. The table gives the positions of carts A and B at different moments (example data).

Draw the $(t, x)$ points of both carts in the same graph and fit a straight line to each. Determine the velocities of the carts from the lines and tell which one moves faster.

When are the carts at the same position? Write this moment in the answer box.

data.caption: Positions of carts A and B (example data)

level2.text:
A robot moves along a straight track, and its position has been measured at certain moments (example data). Between two measurement points the motion is uniform.

Draw the $(t, x)$ graph of the robot and, based on it, the $(t, v)$ graph by drawing the velocity of each time interval. During which time interval does the robot move in the negative direction?

Write in the answer box the velocity of the robot during this interval, with its sign.

The graph shows the position of a cart as a function of time. The cart moves along a straight track: first it moves forward, then it stands still for a moment, and finally it returns part of the way back. Calculate the average speed of the cart over the whole $10\,\text{s}$, that is the distance travelled divided by the elapsed time.

The graph shows the positions of two bodies A and B as a function of time. The motion of both is uniform, and the bodies move along the same straight line. How far apart are the bodies at the moment $t = 6.0\,\text{s}$?

level3.text: A cyclist rides east along a straight road $6.0\,\text{km}$ in $20\,\text{min}$ and then turns straight back, riding the same $6.0\,\text{km}$ west in $30\,\text{min}$. Calculate the average speed over the whole trip, that is the distance travelled divided by the elapsed time. Give the answer in the unit m/s.

Aino and Eeva start walking towards each other at the same time along the same line. Aino starts from the position 0 and walks at a velocity $1.5\,\text{m/s}$ in the positive direction. Eeva starts from the position $90\,\text{m}$ and walks at a velocity $-1.2\,\text{m/s}$. At what position do they meet?

The $(t, x)$ graph of a robot consists of three straight parts: between 0 and $10\,\text{s}$ the position grows from 0 to $30\,\text{m}$, between 10 and $20\,\text{s}$ the robot is at rest and between 20 and $40\,\text{s}$ the position decreases to $10\,\text{m}$. What is the average velocity of the robot over the whole $40\,\text{s}$? Give the answer with its sign.

The motion of a cart was studied with video analysis. The scale of the program was set with a $1.00\,\text{m}$ measuring stick placed beside the track, but the stick was closer to the camera than the track of the cart. The table gives the positions given by the program (example data). The motion of the cart is uniform.

Later a $2.00\,\text{m}$ measuring tape was placed on the track, and the program gave its length as $1.60\,\text{m}$.

Determine from the table the velocity given by the program by fitting a straight line. Correct the velocity with the measuring tape to the true velocity $v$ of the cart. Estimate when the cart would be at the true position $6.0\,\text{m}$, and justify whether the prediction is reliable. Also explain why the scale error is systematic and is not corrected by repeating the measurement.

Write the true velocity of the cart in the answer box.

data.caption: Position of the cart on the scale of the program (example data)

level3.text:
On a highway, a sensor beside the road follows the position of a truck. The table gives the position of the truck on an $x$-axis along the road (example data). The motion of the truck is uniform and in the positive direction.

A police car passes the position $x = 0$ at the moment $t = 8.0\,\text{s}$ and drives in the direction of the truck at a uniform velocity $16\,\text{m/s}$.

Fit a straight line to the measurement points of the truck and write the position of the truck as a function of time. Write the position of the police car as a function of time. Determine at what position the police car catches up with the truck, and justify why this prediction is uncertain when the data of the sensor ends at the moment $t = 40\,\text{s}$.

Write the position where the police car catches up in the answer box.
